requirements.name: Extreme cold
requirements.measure: Coldest monthly minimum 2 m air temperature (NASA POWER T2M_MIN climatology)

requirements.name: Low-angle polar lighting
requirements.measure: Absolute latitude; at or above the polar circle the Sun skims the horizon as at the lunar pole

requirements.name: Impact crater terrain
requirements.measure: Tag impact_crater (confirmed in the Earth Impact Database); volcanic crater = partial

requirements.name: Lava tubes or caves for shelter
Barren, near-lifeless surface
requirements.measure: Tag barren; sparse vegetation = partial (MODIS NDVI is a stretch goal)

requirements.name: Hyperaridity
requirements.measure: Annual precipitation (NASA POWER PRECTOTCORR, mm/day x 365)

requirements.name: High UV exposure
requirements.measure: Peak-month all-sky surface UV index (NASA POWER ALLSKY_SFC_UV_INDEX, 24 h mean)

requirements.name: Low air pressure
requirements.measure: Annual mean surface pressure (NASA POWER PS)

requirements.name: Large daily temperature swing
requirements.measure: Annual mean diurnal 2 m temperature range (NASA POWER T2M_RANGE)

requirements.name: Iron-rich basalt or volcanic terrain
requirements.measure: Tag basalt / volcanic; iron-rich sediments or tephra = partial

requirements.name: Ancient lakebed or evaporites (Jezero-like)
requirements.measure: Tag paleolake / evaporite; hydrothermal or lake sediments = partial

requirements.name: Dust and wind

moon.name: Moon south pole (Shackleton rim / Artemis III candidate regions)
moon.description: Ridges and crater rims near the lunar south pole get near-continuous but grazing sunlight, while nearby permanently shadowed craters are among the coldest places in the Solar System and trap water ice. Surface is anorthositic highland regolith with heavy impact cratering.

compare.M5: Water ice in permanently shadowed craters
compare.M6: Lunar pits/lava tubes known at lower latitudes
compare.R4: Swings of > 100 °C between light and shadow

citations.label: Paige et al. 2010, Science (Diviner cold traps)

mars.name: Mars, Jezero Crater (Perseverance landing site)
mars.description: A 45 km impact crater that once held a lake, with a preserved river delta, lakebed sediments and a basaltic, olivine- and carbonate-bearing floor. Thin CO2 atmosphere, no ozone layer, large daily temperature swings and frequent dust devils.

facts.label: Elevation
facts.value: about −2.6 km relative to Mars datum

facts.label: Geology
facts.value: basaltic floor (Máaz), olivine cumulate (Séítah), delta and lake sediments

compare.M4: Jezero itself is a 45 km impact crater
compare.M6: Lava tubes and pits on Tharsis
compare.R7: 2–10 m/s, dust devils, global dust storms

sites.name: Atacama Desert (Yungay)
sites.description: Hyperarid core of the Atacama; soils so dry and oxidizing that Viking-style life-detection experiments returned Mars-like results.

sites.name: Haughton Crater (Devon Island)
sites.description: 23 km impact crater in a polar desert; home of the NASA Haughton-Mars Project and the FMARS habitat.

sites.name: Death Valley
sites.description: Hot, dry basin with Pleistocene Lake Manly evaporites and the Ubehebe volcanic crater; used to test Mars rover and instrument concepts.

sites.name: McMurdo Dry Valleys
sites.description: Coldest, driest ice-free terrain on Earth; ground ice, saline ponds and polygons used as a Mars analog for decades.

sites.name: Mauna Kea
sites.description: High basaltic volcano with tephra fields; site of NASA/PISCES lunar ISRU field tests in 2010 and 2012.

sites.name: Mars Desert Research Station
sites.description: Mars Society simulation habitat amid red Jurassic sediments near Hanksville, Utah.

sites.name: Rio Tinto
sites.description: Acidic, iron-rich river system analogous to Meridiani jarosite deposits; NASA MARTE drilling site.

sites.name: Svalbard (Bockfjord)
sites.description: Arctic volcanic complex with carbonate globules like those in Martian meteorite ALH84001; AMASE expedition site.

sites.name: Meteor Crater
sites.description: Young 1.2 km impact crater in Arizona used for Apollo astronaut geology training.

sites.name: Craters of the Moon
sites.description: Basaltic lava fields and tubes in Idaho; Apollo 14 geology training and NASA FINESSE field site.

sites.name: Lanzarote lava tubes
sites.description: La Corona lava tube system; used for ESA PANGAEA and CAVES astronaut training.

sites.name: Iceland lava fields (Askja)
sites.description: Basaltic caldera and tephra plains in the highlands where Apollo astronauts trained in 1965 and 1967.

sites.name: Ladakh (Tso Kar)
sites.description: High-altitude saline lake basin in a cold desert; studied as a Mars analog for evaporites and periglacial landforms.

sites.name: Qaidam Basin (Dalangtan)
sites.description: Hyperarid, high-altitude playa with sulfate and chloride evaporites; studied as a Mars analog.

sites.name: Pavilion Lake
sites.description: Lake with freshwater microbialites; NASA/CSA Pavilion Lake Research Project tested EVA and science operations.

sites.name: Black Point Lava Flow
sites.description: Basaltic flow in northern Arizona used by NASA Desert RATS for rover and spacesuit field tests.

sites.name: Lonar Crater
sites.description: Rare impact crater in Deccan basalt with a saline, alkaline lake; a close analog for craters in Martian basalt.

sites.name: Rann of Kutch
sites.description: Vast seasonal salt marsh; flat evaporite plains comparable to Martian chloride deposits.

sites.name: Spiti Valley
sites.description: Cold Himalayan desert with periglacial landforms and Tethyan sediments.

sites.name: Puga Valley
sites.description: High-altitude hot springs with borax and sulfur deposits in a permafrost setting.

sites.name: Deccan Traps (Mahabaleshwar)
sites.description: Thick flood-basalt sequence, a compositional analog for Martian and lunar mare basalts.

sites.name: Changthang Plateau (Hanle)
sites.description: High cold desert above 4,300 m with saline lakes, low pressure and strong UV.

sites.name: Dasht-e Lut
sites.description: One of the hottest, driest surfaces on Earth, with giant yardangs carved by wind like those on Mars.

sites.name: Danakil Depression (Dallol)
sites.description: Hyperacid, hypersaline hydrothermal field below sea level; tests the limits of habitability.

sites.name: Erta Ale
sites.description: Active basaltic shield volcano with a persistent lava lake in the Afar desert.

sites.name: Namib Desert (Gobabeb)
sites.description: Ancient coastal fog desert with gravel plains and large dune fields.

sites.name: Gobi Desert (Flaming Cliffs)
sites.description: Cold, windy desert with red Cretaceous sediments and wide seasonal temperature swings.

sites.name: Puna de Atacama (Antofalla)
sites.description: High volcanic plateau with salars and basaltic cones, intense UV and low pressure.

sites.name: Salar de Uyuni
sites.description: World's largest salt flat, the remnant of Pleistocene lakes on the Altiplano.

sites.name: Licancabur (Altiplano)
sites.description: 5,900 m volcano with one of the highest lakes on Earth; extreme UV and low pressure.

sites.name: Kerguelen Islands
sites.description: Remote, windswept sub-Antarctic flood-basalt archipelago.

sites.name: Ross Island (Mount Erebus)
sites.description: Polar volcano with fumarolic ice caves, permafrost and an active lava lake.

sites.name: Greenland ice-free margin (Kangerlussuaq)
sites.description: Ice-free terrain at the edge of the Greenland ice sheet with permafrost and glacial outwash.

sites.name: Kamchatka (Tolbachik)
sites.description: Fresh basaltic lava fields and tephra plains with lava tubes from the 2012–13 eruption.

sites.name: Undara lava tubes
sites.description: Among the longest lava tube systems on Earth, formed ~190,000 years ago.

sites.name: Pilbara (Dresser Formation)
sites.description: 3.5-billion-year-old hydrothermal sediments with some of Earth's oldest evidence of life.

sites.name: Kati Thanda–Lake Eyre
sites.description: Australia's largest salt lake, usually dry, in the arid interior.

sites.name: Wolfe Creek Crater
sites.description: Well-preserved 880 m meteorite crater in the Great Sandy Desert.

sites.name: Gosses Bluff
sites.description: Eroded central uplift of a 142-million-year-old impact structure.

sites.name: Popigai Crater
sites.description: 100 km impact structure in Siberian permafrost, rich in impact diamonds.

sites.name: Lake El'gygytgyn
sites.description: 3.6-million-year-old Arctic impact crater lake with a continuous sediment record.

sites.name: Pingualuit Crater
sites.description: Young 3.4 km impact crater in the Nunavik tundra.

sites.name: Manicouagan Crater
sites.description: Large impact structure with impact melt over anorthositic target rocks.

sites.name: Mistastin Lake Crater
sites.description: One of very few terrestrial impact craters in anorthosite, the dominant lunar highland rock.

sites.name: Stillwater Complex
sites.description: Layered intrusion with anorthosite used as feedstock for NASA lunar highland regolith simulants.

sites.name: Merriam Crater cinders
sites.description: Basaltic cinder deposit near Flagstaff, source of the JSC-1 lunar regolith simulant.

sites.name: Lava Beds
sites.description: More than 700 lava tube caves, several with perennial ice.

sites.name: El Malpais
sites.description: Young basalt flows with lava tubes and ice caves in New Mexico.

sites.name: Jeju lava tubes (Manjanggul)
sites.description: Large, accessible basaltic lava tube system on a volcanic island.

sites.name: Harrat Khaybar
sites.description: Arid basaltic lava field with cinder cones and lava tubes such as Umm Jirsan.

sites.name: Rub' al Khali
sites.description: The largest continuous sand desert on Earth.

sites.name: Tibesti (Emi Koussi)
sites.description: Large shield volcano with a summit caldera in the central Sahara.

sites.name: Kamil Crater
sites.description: Pristine 45 m iron-meteorite crater in the hyperarid Western Desert.

sites.name: Lop Nur
sites.description: Dried salt lake with yardangs in the Tarim Basin; one of the driest places in Asia.

sites.name: Ngari (western Tibet)
sites.description: High, cold, dry plateau with saline lakes and periglacial terrain.

sites.name: Axel Heiberg Island
sites.description: Perennial cold saline springs flowing through thick permafrost.

sites.name: Allan Hills
sites.description: Blue-ice field where Martian meteorite ALH84001 was found.

sites.name: Ojos del Salado
sites.description: The highest volcano on Earth; dry, cold, low-pressure summit region with permafrost.

sites.name: Kilimanjaro summit
sites.description: Equatorial volcanic summit above 5,800 m with low pressure and intense UV.

sites.name: Lac Assal
sites.description: Hypersaline lake in basaltic rift terrain, 155 m below sea level.

sites.name: Wadi Rum
sites.description: Red sandstone desert valleys often used to depict Mars on film.

sites.name: Ka'u Desert (Kilauea)
sites.description: Barren basalt and tephra fields downwind of Kilauea's acid gas plume.

sites.name: Fernandina Island
sites.description: Young, active basaltic shield volcano in the Galápagos.

sites.name: Salar de Atacama
sites.description: Large salt flat on the edge of the hyperarid Atacama.

sites.name: Batagaika Crater
sites.description: Huge thaw slump exposing hundreds of thousands of years of Siberian ground ice.

sites.name: Pinacate volcanic field
sites.description: Basaltic field with large maar craters in the Sonoran Desert.

sites.name: Cuatro Ciénegas
sites.description: Desert basin with gypsum dunes and living stromatolites.

sites.name: White Sands
sites.description: The largest gypsum dune field on Earth, like Mars' north-polar gypsum dunes.

sites.name: Monturaqui Crater
sites.description: Small impact crater in the hyperarid, high Atacama.

sites.name: Wabar Craters
sites.description: Iron-meteorite craters in the sand sea of the Rub' al Khali.

sites.name: Hoggar (Atakor)
sites.description: Volcanic highland of basalt plateaus and phonolite spires in the central Sahara.
